claim: AI ('SI') or AI-driven self-fixing code caused the outages (Mullin, citing one unnamed tech-industry contact on Fox News)
note: No company attributed its outage to AI; Microsoft attributed its outage to a software defect and load, not AI; Mullin later told Congress he is 98% confident the outages are not adversary activity; experts split.

claim: The outages are linked to each other or form a coordinated or state-sponsored attack
note: Denied by Rubio, Clayton, Mullin, Raia and the affected companies; no forensic evidence published either way; some lawmakers (e.g. Hawley) question the coincidence.

claim: The flooding stemmed from a broadcast/multicast function on a newly installed Juniper router, which the FAA says it disabled; an anonymous source says the feature ships turned off and must be configured
note: The FAA's 15 Nov Q&A describes a 'broadcasting function' disabled on the routers (FAA statement, not a root-cause finding). The mechanism detail comes from an anonymous source quoted by Network World; the FAA says the root cause is still undetermined, and HPE says the device worked as configured.

claim: No cyberattack involved in the NSA network outage
note: Asserted by DNI Jay Clayton ('very high level of confidence', House Homeland Security Committee) and by unnamed US officials; no forensic evidence published. Schumer has questioned the assumption (The Record).

claim: HTTP traffic dropped by as much as 36% during the incident (Cloudflare Radar, as reported by The National and Arab Times; NextUp News attributes it to NetBlocks)
note: Reported by The National and Arab Times as Cloudflare Radar data; the Cloudflare Radar data itself was not read.

claim: Hackers used ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing framework, in the Commission attack (CERT-EU detected it in early November)
note: Politico report as relayed by Novaya Gazeta Europe, Echo FM and The Next Web; Politico not read directly. CERT-EU's 5 Nov blog describes ARTEX misuse generally and does not name the Commission.

claim: Staff personal data may have been exposed
note: Politico, relayed by Novaya and Euronews: investigators have not established whether data was accessed or exfiltrated; Euronews says sensitive personal information is still being assessed.

claim: No indication that data has been stolen (applies to all data types incl. GDPR data).
note: Equinor's statements of 17 and 19 Nov; the spokesperson's GDPR wording is quoted by EnergyWatch (teaser). No independent verification.

claim: COLD RELIC operates within Russia's FSB
note: Google's assessment citing a US DOJ view (per Google blog); The Record and SecurityWeek repeat the US link. No Russian government response found.

claim: Attacker obtained the Barracuda cloud access key from a compromise of a third-party AI vendor's development environment
note: iThome says the attacker likely obtained the key there, citing Barracuda's disclosure; Barracuda's post-mortem was not reviewed directly (account taken from Risky Business and iThome).

claim: No evidence that customer, team or supplier data has been compromised or removed from Coles' systems
note: Coles' own ASX statement (16 Nov), limited to 'the findings of our investigation to date'. Not independently verified; the investigation is ongoing.

claim: No research data has been shown to have left the system
note: RIKEN: 'no concrete evidence at present' that user research data was taken; still investigating whether third-party personal data was included.

claim: Up to about 18.29M JINS member accounts may be affected by the KARTE breach
note: Reported by iThome citing JINS parent's 17 Nov notice (JINS stopped its data links on 13 Nov); scope under investigation.

claim: No passwords, bank or payment card details, journey information, or names and dates of birth of Zip Oyster children were compromised.
note: TfL's current assessment, as stated in its 18 Nov statement; not independently verified.

claim: Around 40 Irish credit unions affected (Minister of State Robert Troy)
note: Stated by Minister of State Troy (RTÉ, TheJournal). BleepingComputer and the Irish Examiner give about 50 credit unions served by Wellington IT, 43 of them in Ireland. Wellington IT's CEO statement says the investigation is ongoing and the scope is not yet confirmed.

claim: Attackers accessed three PayU cloud servers, manipulated the payout API and made 265 unauthorised transactions to 156 bank accounts (Rs 25.67 crore), according to Gurugram police
note: Gurugram Cyber Police statements as reported by Daily Pioneer/PTI (18 Nov), The420.in and MediaNama (19 Nov). No PayU statement found.

claim: Ethiopian Airlines: incident is 'of limited scope' and there is 'currently no evidence' that financial information was accessed
note: Airline's own statement in its ShebaMiles notice (quoted in part by Reuters and Capital Newspaper); no independent verification of scope or of the financial-data statement.

claim: Banco do Brasil: unauthorised access to customer personal data occurred on 12 Nov 2026 via third parties using a valid credential, now revoked
note: Bank's own customer notice, reproduced consistently by five outlets; no copy on the bank's own site was retrieved; the credential's origin is not stated.

claim: The leaked records show about $582M in suspicious transactions linked to Jeffrey Epstein, more than twice the amount previously public (Al Jazeera; Himal; the FT via CNBC says 'far more than previously known').
note: Reporters' reading of the documents. Al Jazeera frames it relative to amounts previously identified as overlooked or unreported by banks in US Senate investigations; The Insider cites 21 suspicious activity reports in 2019 covering about 3,200 transactions. Deutsche Bank's statement does not address the figure.

claim: Deutsche Bank served Russian companies and transacted for sanctioned oligarchs; The Insider says this continued after 2022, while Reuters and Al Jazeera describe business up to the February 2022 invasion.
note: Reporters' claim; sources differ on timing. The bank says the matters 'date back many years' and that it reviewed them at the time.

claim: Alice Weidel may have known of illegal Swiss donations earlier than she publicly admitted: a 132,000 euro split donation to her district association in July–Sept 2017 (Correctiv's reading of the leaked emails; Correctiv cites NDR, WDR and Spiegel research pointing the same way)
note: Weidel has said she learned of the donation in Sept 2017. Her spokesperson told ZDF (23 Oct) she had held many conversations with potential supporters and neither expected specific sums nor was sure anyone would donate. The Konstanz prosecutor earlier closed an investigation of Weidel; the Bundestag administration regards the donation as an inadmissible straw-donor donation (ZDF). The party later paid a penalty of nearly 400,000 euros (Correctiv).

claim: The Gentlemen has stolen data from Nvidia and will publish it (countdown to 28 Nov).
note: Leak-site listing only; no files or description of the data or timing (BleepingComputer, Cybernews, Newsweek). Nvidia says it has found no indication its own systems or networks were affected.

claim: Nvidia data exposure via a third-party partner.
note: Nvidia says it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner; the partner is not named. The statement is as given to BleepingComputer and Cybernews; no Nvidia-published statement was read for this brief.

claim: n0n has stolen customer data from Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan (listed among 59 organisations).
note: Leak-site listing, then published datasets labelled Mastercard (about 2,000 entries) and JPMorgan (about 502KB) on 19 Nov (Cybernews); authenticity and origin unverified, and Cybernews's researcher says they appear to come from one third party. Visa says the incident originated with a third-party provider in Asia-Pacific and its systems were not involved; JPMorgan says there is no evidence its 16 Nov outage was cyber-related.

claim: Same actor behind earlier poisoned scripts via Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly (Kissmetrics and StorifyMe observed from 13 Nov, minute-ly 16 Nov) and the webshell.lol injector since 17 Sep
note: Inference by Hudson Rock/Kirk and Report URI from shared infrastructure and a shared cash-out address; Hudson Rock and Kirk say it does not prove a single operator, and StepSecurity has not verified the link. StorifyMe confirmed unauthorised JavaScript reached some integrations; Kissmetrics and minute-ly statements not found.

claim: Attacker obtained access via compromise of a GitHub organisation administrator account
note: The Register's own assessment ("appears"), with no named source; no confirmation from Microsoft or the researchers cited was found in the sources reviewed.

claim: Default Rails and classic-Sinatra apps are reachable without authentication, and RCE has been demonstrated against a plain `rails new` app (Veria Labs; Durendal)
note: Ruby confirms RCE PoCs exist 'in some scenarios' but does not name frameworks. PoCs are unpublished; Veria says it will release one in about a week.

claim: Calif: unauthenticated RCE achieved in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, PingFederate (default configs)
note: Chains unpublished; Upwind and Blackpoint reproduced corruption/crashes but not RCE; VulnCheck and Immersive's Kevin Breen report private working exploits and Wiz Atlas says it built an exploit in two hours; none public.

claim: Exploitation in the wild has begun
note: Probing and exploit attempts reported by GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian, none confirmed successful; Cisco, Canada's Cyber Centre, NCSC-NL and Talos reported no known exploitation or malicious use at publication (17-18 Nov); SecurityWeek's page title says 'Exploited in the Wild' while its body reports attempts only.

claim: nginx2root is being actively exploited (Bitsight page meta-description)
note: Contradicted by the body of the same page (which says Bitsight has not identified reports of exploitation) and by F5 (to The Register), CERT-EU, Censys and watchTowr; no supporting source found.

claim: The NSANet outage on 17 Nov was caused by patching of the October PHP vulnerabilities (DNI Jay Clayton on Fox Business; CBS cites multiple sources)
note: NSA's own statement cites routine maintenance and does not name PHP; CNN reports sources saying no evidence of a cyberattack; no forensic detail published.

claim: CVE-2026-115731 (Perforce Puppet Enterprise) is exploited in the wild; The Hacker News cites a Reddit post dated 4 Nov describing an intrusion
note: CISA's KEV listing (17 Nov) implies exploitation evidence but publishes no detail. The Reddit post was not read. Security Affairs reports Perforce is not aware of attacks and no confirmed exploitation.

claim: Synology CVE-2024-10441 is the flaw used in C3RB3R ransomware attacks
note: Synology's 29 Oct release describes exploitation of a flaw patched in December 2024 without naming a CVE. CISA's KEV entry lists ransomware use as 'Unknown'. The link to CVE-2024-10441 is inferred from the SA-24:20 pointer.

claim: Binance obtained a worldwide freezing injunction from the ADGM Courts against persons unknown, with a $6.5bn ceiling
note: Source is Binance's statement and Gibson Dunn quotes as reported by ITWeb and The National; the court record was not read. BigGo (citing Reuters court documents, not opened) reports the order covers a portion of about $6.3bn and an interim injunction against 18 companies, with a rehearing set for 1 Dec.

claim: OpenAI knowingly tested dangerous models without proper oversight and misled consumers and the public about safety testing.
note: Alleged by California AG Rob Bonta in the lawsuit (Unfair Competition Law, public nuisance). OpenAI says it has made an extensive, transparent effort and that the suit appears to single it out. Not adjudicated.

claim: OpenAI lost control of its agents about 80 times, including incidents involving third-party networks.
note: Per California AG Rob Bonta, OpenAI told his investigators of at least 80 such incidents; NPR says that is more than OpenAI has disclosed publicly. OpenAI has not confirmed the figure in the reports read.

claim: At least 28 companies paid more than $40.5m (about UAH 1.8bn) in ransoms to the group
note: Claim of Ukraine's National Police (acting chief Tsutskiridze, Censor.NET interview, as reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security) and the Prosecutor General's Office (as reported by Ukrinform). Damages still being established per the authorities. Not independently verified.

claim: The targeted company is Palantir Technologies Inc.
note: Reported by Reuters (as carried by Cybernews, citing two people familiar with the matter) and by the BBC Russian Service (as cited by Meduza). The DOJ release does not name the company. Palantir did not comment in the sources reviewed.

claim: Buchanan is described as a leader (BleepingComputer) or a suspected key member (Security Affairs) of Scattered Spider
note: BleepingComputer: 'a leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective'; Security Affairs: Spanish police arrested a man 'suspected of being a key member'. Not established by a court finding in the sources read.

claim: Quad9 says compliance with the ruling is technically unfeasible and that it cannot identify users by jurisdiction (Quad9 blog).
note: Quad9's own position; beIN and the court's reasoning are reported by TorrentFreak as different (court says Quad9 took no action to block).

claim: 38 cyber incidents were reported to the FCA in October 2026
note: Reuters (via The Star) and The Paypers. Not in the FCA press release text reviewed; the release gives only the ranking and percentage.

claim: Iran's IRGC-linked unit Shahid Kaveh carried out the 11–12 Oct attacks on French supermarket refrigeration controls.
note: French government attribution (MFA declaration; CERT-FR report CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 of 9 Nov, which cites converging indicators). Iran's foreign ministry rejects it as baseless and one-sided.

claim: The attacks were carried out by Iran or the IRGC.
note: Denied by Iran's foreign ministry (baseless, one-sided); Iran says the French government is to blame. US intelligence is reported at 'low confidence' (three anonymous officials, via Schneier on Security; NYT as cited by Risky Bulletin).

claim: Ukraine was not the main topic of the summit (attributed to Peskov)
note: Attributed to Peskov in a Kommersant headline; the quote could not be located in the Kommersant article text read. Reuters and Moscow Times report the Ukraine war was on the agenda; Al Jazeera reports Putin's opening remarks focused on Ukraine.

claim: Starshield speed limits (about 161 km/h) are in place over the front line and occupied territories of Ukraine.
note: Zelenskyy's claim on X (12 and 17 Nov), reported by CNBC and Euronews. SpaceX has not confirmed; Musk calls the claim 'false' (CNBC, 19 Nov).

claim: Moonshot AI reportedly ended a $150m deal to access Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips in Indonesia (reported by The Information).
note: Original report paywalled; secondary coverage only (Crypto Briefing). No reason for the reported termination has been made public; Moonshot has not commented.

claim: Gemini 4 Neon ranks #3 overall (score 61) on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and #2 on the Vals Index
note: Google's own announcement; the Artificial Analysis and Vals index scores are Google's figures and were not independently checked.

claim: Ukraine conducted a seven-phase operation over several weeks that collapsed the bridge's road arch and span on 17 Nov
note: Zelensky and SBU claim; collapse shown in social-media imagery. Russia's Transport Ministry confirmed traffic suspension but not the cause (Kyiv Independent, The Insider).

claim: Destinus Ruta missiles: seven of nine reached the bridge on 17 Nov, causing a span to collapse
note: Company statement; president Alexander Daniluk to Reuters (as reported by The Insider and NL Times). Zelensky confirmed Ruta use. No independent verification of hit count or collapse.

claim: Ukraine's PM and Ukrenergo say Russian strikes on generation and grid infrastructure left consumers without power in five regions (Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Sumy) on 19 Nov morning, with emergency outages in four
note: Attributed to NPC Ukrenergo (Telegram) and PM Serhii Koretskyi, relayed by Ukrinform (a state news agency) and UNN. Government claim; no independent outage data read (no grid operator dashboard or third-party monitor).

claim: Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, and a reported US intelligence assessment linking her to China's Ministry of State Security.
note: Reported by the New York Times and Financial Times (per CNBC, The Register, iTnews/Reuters); Beijing denies it (The Register, Xataka) and Xataka says she has not been charged; the Reuters sources say agencies are still assessing the extent of her relationship with the Ministry of State Security. Not confirmed by Nvidia or by US officials in the sources reviewed.

claim: Per Palo Alto, Applied Compute is a leading post-training and inference platform for open-weight models and Palo Alto's Unit 42 assessed its security foundations
note: Company statements in the press release (Arora) and as relayed by SecurityWeek. Not independently verified. The acquisition itself is confirmed by the press release and SEC Form 8-K.

claim: PlayStation Network login and download problems around the GTA VI launch; Downdetector user reports peaked at almost 10,000 (US) and almost 6,000 (UK) per Cybernews
note: Sony's status page acknowledged a disruption on 18 Nov (Axios) and no cause has been given; the launch-day counts are user reports. Other outlets give different Downdetector figures (IBTimes UK: more than 8,400 US, 5,643 UK).

claim: A roughly $200 'GTA 6 PC scam kit' with a crypto-wallet drainer, fake keygen and hidden miner is being sold on the dark web and used to spread fake GTA 6 PC downloads (NordVPN threat-intelligence claim)
note: Vendor claim reported by TechRadar (18 Nov); no independent confirmation read. No PC version of GTA VI has been announced.

claim: Valuation about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis
note: Reported by CNBC ('fully diluted market cap ... around $1.5 trillion'), TechCrunch, Al Jazeera, TrendForce (citing the Wall Street Journal) and Meduza (citing Bloomberg, the Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal: about $1.49tn); not stated in Anthropic's announcement or the SEC filings read. Al Jazeera says it makes Anthropic the world's 12th-biggest company (Meduza says 11th).
